newsitem.title: THAILAND: Cambodia opposition says election illegal.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia opposition says election illegal.

text.p: Cambodian opposition politicians on Wednesday condemned the approval of Foreign Minister Ung Huot as the country's new first prime minister as illegal and a violation of the constitution.

Cambodia'a National Assembly voted to approve Ung Huot's nomination to replace Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who was ousted from his position by strongman Hun Sen after the Second Prime Minister led a bloody power grab in early July. Ranariddh was out of the country at the time and has not returned.

Assembly officials said on Wednesday 86 members of parliament voted in favour of the motion, four voted against it and there were six abstentions and three spoiled ballots. Eighty votes were needed for the motion to pass.
Members of the Union of Cambodian Democrats (UCD), a movement formed by Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC and three opposition parties, condemned Ung Huot's appointment as illegal.

"The appointment today by the National Assembly, in an atmosphere of intimidation and fear, of Mr Ung Huot as 'First Prime Minister' is totally illegal and can mislead only people who do not pay any attention at all to the rule of law," said a UCD statement signed by opposition leader Sam Rainsy.
Sam Rainsy, leader of the Khmer Nation Party, is in Bangkok trying to build support for the opposition.
He told Reuters King Norodom Sihanouk, who is in Beijing for medical treatment, did not recognise Ung Huot and supported the opposition movement.
"We have the support of the king," he said in an interview. "By saying publicly as he did that he wouldn't recognise Ung Huot it should block the whole process."
Sihanouk, Ranariddh's father, has said he would not recognise Ung Huot's nomination as prime minister, saying the position belonged to his son.
Sam Rainsy said he expected the King might make some sort of statement following the vote in Phnom Penh.

The UCD statement said under normal procedures the King must first designate the leader of the main political party in the National Assembly to form the Royal Government. Then a candidate designated by the king must be approved by the assembly.

"In the case of Mr Ung Huot's appointment, the first step of the government formation was totally disregarded. In this strange selection and appointment process, Mr Hun Sen, the leader of the July putsch, effectively took up the role of the King," the statement said.
Members of the FUNCINPEC party still in the country nominated Ung Huot to succeed the prince as co-premier.
Hun Sen backed Ung Huot's nomination.
After taking sole power, Hun Sen said he wanted to keep his Cambodia People's Party's coalition with FUNCINPEC in palace and said the FUNCINPEC should select a new first prime minister.
Ranariddh, who left Cambodia just before he was overthrown, has been calling for opposition to Hun Sen from abroad.
He formed the UCD with a group of FUNCINPEC and opposition politicians who had fled Cambodia in the wake of the coup.
He has also expelled Ung Huot from the party.
The National Assembly on Wednesday voted to strip Ranariddh of his parliamentary immunity.
